scope: Additive current Dragon Duke Royal Rampage trap-damage mitigation for the existing isolated-flying-unit predicate. Equipment remains excluded.

sources.title: July Balance Update
facts: Dragon Duke receives another cut to trap damage reduction.
sources.limitations: The official note does not publish the resulting numeric reduction.

sources.title: Dragon Duke Guide: How to Unlock, Upgrade, and Use Clash of Clans' Newest Hero
facts: The July update changed the isolated Dragon Duke's trap reduction from 40 percent to 20 percent.
The reduction applies during Royal Rampage.
sources.limitations: Community guide. It attributes the balance change to Supercell but is the source of the exact post-July number.

sources.title: Clash of Clans tweaks Dragon units, Logger and equipment in July
facts: The July balance change cuts Dragon Duke trap damage reduction from 40 percent to 20 percent.
sources.limitations: Secondary report. It corroborates the exact post-July percentage but does not define per-trap collision timing.

rage_trap_damage_multiplier.derivation: A 20 percent reduction leaves 80 percent of incoming trap damage.

support.note: Core applies the 0.8 incoming-damage multiplier only when the existing Royal Rampage isolated-flying predicate is true and the source entity is a trap.

changed_values.previous_state: Post-July trap reduction was an explicit unknown.
changed_values.replacement: Isolated Royal Rampage takes 20 percent less trap damage, materialized as an incoming multiplier of 0.8.
changed_values.justification: The exact value is corroborated by two dated secondary reports while Supercell independently confirms the July reduction and unchanged rage.

items: whether all hidden-trap categories share identical client application order
projectile or contact launch and collision timing
isolation transition ordering beyond Core logical units
battlefield sprite, scale and asset rights

conclusion: The known current 20 percent Royal Rampage trap mitigation is applied through shared Core damage resolution. It remains limited to trap-origin damage and the already documented isolated-flying predicate.
